# Fly.io — Style Reference

> Hand-inked balloons drifting over lavender paper, one coral ticket in hand. Medium-weight book serif headlines, plum-tinted ink on white and lilac bands, hairlines in pale heather, and a single coral pill that buys the ride.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Fly.io speaks a storybook-infrastructure language: a platform for hardware-isolated VMs and agent sandboxes, narrated like an illustrated picture book. The canvas is Paper Canvas #ffffff. It alternates with Lilac Mist #faf8ff bands, pastel Frosted Tile #e3f2f8 and Lavender Tile #ece9ff cards, and two night-plum floors: #231850 for feature bands and #191034 for the footer. The chromatic budget is two hues. Ember Signal #f86d60 is rationed to the sign-up and start-free pills, while Violet Ink #6d28d9 carries italic headline clauses, links, arrows and stat numerals. Every neutral is purple-tinted, from Plum Ink #281950 down to Lilac Hairline #e4def7, so not one true gray exists. Hierarchy runs on a Mackinac serif locked at weight 500 with -0.025em tracking. It steps from 26 to 56px on a roughly Major Third ratio, set against Fricolage Grotesque at fractional weights from 325 to 575. Shapes are pills and 24px cards lifted by plum-tinted shadows. It reads as a children's atlas of the cloud rather than a terminal dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page canvas, the white secondary pill and the mega-menu panel, with 20 background uses — the neutral stage that lets the pastel tiles and illustrations carry the color. |
| Lilac Mist | `#faf8ff` | `--color-lilac-mist` | Alternating section bands behind the integration grid and trust row — a 2% violet lift that separates sections without a single divider line. |
| Lavender Tile | `#ece9ff` | `--color-lavender-tile` | Fill for the lower row of use-case cards and tinted chips — a pastel surface that reads as paper stock rather than a UI panel. |
| Frosted Tile | `#e3f2f8` | `--color-frosted-tile` | Fill for the Web Apps and APIs cards, echoing the hero sky gradient — the only cool-blue surface, so keep it to card fills and do not use it for text or borders. |
| Plum Night | `#231850` | `--color-plum-night` | The "Use the tech you love" feature band and its dark logo grid, with 9 uses — the inverted surface that gives the scroll a night chapter. |
| Plum Basement | `#191034` | `--color-plum-basement` | The footer floor beneath Plum Night — one step darker so the page ends on its deepest tone. |
| Plum Ink | `#281950` | `--color-plum-ink` | Headlines, card titles, nav links and coral-button labels, with 54 text uses — the workhorse ink, purple rather than black, so the serif reads warm instead of stark. |
| Slate Body | `#5b4f78` | `--color-slate-body` | Paragraphs, card descriptions and mega-menu captions, with 33 uses — a desaturated plum that keeps body copy in the same family as the headlines. |
| Pewter Label | `#6d5f8f` | `--color-pewter-label` | Uppercase eyebrow labels such as COMPUTE, STORAGE and NETWORKING in the mega menu — a micro-label tone that sits between body and caption. |
| Heather Caption | `#a39ac1` | `--color-heather-caption` | Footer links, footer body copy and muted captions, with 22 uses — legible on Plum Basement while staying quiet on white. Do not use it for body copy on white. |
| Lilac Hairline | `#e4def7` | `--color-lilac-hairline` | Logo-grid dividers, data-list rules and panel borders, with 12 border uses — a tinted 1px line that structures without drawing a box. |
| Violet Ink | `#6d28d9` | `--color-violet-ink` | Italic hero clauses, "See all integrations" links, list arrows and stat numerals, with 12 text and 8 fill uses — the emphasis hue. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Ember Signal | `#f86d60` | `--color-ember-signal` | The Start free and Sign Up pills, with 3 uses on the page — the only warm saturated fill in the UI, which is exactly why it converts. Do not use it for icons, links or illustrations. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Mackinac — a medium-weight book serif that carries every headline and numeral · `--font-mackinac`

- **Substitute:** Fraunces at 450 with SOFT 0 and WONK 0 (Fraunces draws heavier than its number, so drop one step), Newsreader Display at 500, Source Serif 4 Display at 500. Mackinac 500 renders close to a book Regular, so match that visual weight rather than a Medium, and require a true italic for the violet clause.
- **Weights:** 500
- **Sizes:** 23px, 26px, 32px, 40px, 44px, 48px, 56px
- **Line height:** 1.08, 1.15, 1.25, 1.35
- **Letter spacing:** -1.68px at 56px, -1.44px at 48px, -1.1px at 44px, -1px at 40px, -0.8px at 32px, -0.65px at 26px, -0.575px at 23px
- **Role:** A single weight across seven sizes is deliberate: hierarchy comes from size and italics, not boldness, and that is the anti-convention move against the 700-weight sans headlines of most developer platforms. Tracking holds at -0.025em through the mid sizes and tightens to -0.03em at 48 and 56px, compacting the display lines into editorial blocks. The 26, 32, 44, 56 progression averages a 1.29 step, a loose Major Third. Pairing a literary serif with VM provisioning is the thesis: compute told as a storybook.

### Fricolage Grotesque — a variable grotesk at fractional weights for all UI and body copy · `--font-fricolage-grotesque`

- **Substitute:** Bricolage Grotesque at matching weights of 325, 450, 500 and 575 (the open-source parent of this face, with the same quirky ink traps), DM Sans at 400 for the 325 body and 500 for the 450 UI, Inter at 400 for body and 500 for UI. Fricolage 325 draws close to a Regular 380, so Inter 300 would read too thin.
- **Weights:** 325, 350, 450, 500, 575
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14.5px, 15px, 15.5px, 17px, 19px
- **Line height:** 1.25, 1.5, 1.65
- **Letter spacing:** 0.96px at 12px uppercase 500 (0.08em), 0.6px at 12px uppercase 575 (0.05em), 0 at every other size
- **Role:** Fractional weights are the tell: 325 for reading copy, 450 for interactive labels and 500 for emphasis. That is three steps inside the space where most systems ship one, so the UI gains hierarchy without gaining weight. Half-pixel sizes (14.5px, 15.5px) are tuned for optical fit against the serif rather than taken from a 4px grid. Uppercase tracking appears only at 12px, so micro-labels are the only spaced type in the system.

### ui-monospace — the system mono for the single command-line moment · `--font-ui-monospace`

- **Substitute:** JetBrains Mono at 400, IBM Plex Mono at 400, Geist Mono at 400.
- **Weights:** 325
- **Sizes:** 17px
- **Line height:** 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at 17px
- **Role:** One element uses it, at 17px and weight 325, set to body size so code reads as a sentence rather than a technical sidebar. Its scarcity is intentional, because a developer platform that hides its terminal keeps the picture-book tone intact.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Fricolage Grotesque | 500 | 12px | 1.5 | 0.96px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Fricolage Grotesque | 450 | 14.5px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Fricolage Grotesque | 325 | 15px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Fricolage Grotesque | 325 | 17px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Fricolage Grotesque | 325 | 19px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Mackinac | 500 | 23px | 1.35 | -0.575px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Mackinac | 500 | 26px | 1.25 | -0.65px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Mackinac | 500 | 32px | 1.25 | -0.8px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Mackinac | 500 | 44px | 1.08 | -1.1px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Mackinac | 500 | 56px | 1.15 | -1.68px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Mackinac at weight 500 with -0.025em tracking (-1.1px at 44px) — the medium serif is the storybook voice, and a single weight keeps hierarchy carried by size.
- Turn the second clause of hero headlines into italic Mackinac in #6d28d9 Violet Ink — the violet italic is the signature move and gives one emotional beat per page.
- Use purple-tinted neutrals for all text, with #281950 for titles, #5b4f78 for body and #a39ac1 for captions — tinted ink is non-negotiable because it ties copy to the illustrations.
- Reserve #f86d60 Ember Signal for at most one pill per viewport, sized at 48px height with a 9999px radius — scarcity makes coral read as the ticket, not as decoration.
- Lift content cards with the md shadow (0 16px 40px -20px at 14% plum) and a 24px radius — the negative spread pools shadow under the card like paper on a desk.
- Separate sections with surface shifts between #ffffff, #faf8ff and #231850 at 96px gaps — tonal banding replaces dividers and keeps the page rhythm calm.
- Write body copy in Fricolage Grotesque at weight 325 and 17px with 1.5 line height — the light grotesk lets the serif headlines carry all the visual weight.

### Don't

- Don't bold headlines to 700 or switch them to a sans — a heavy grotesk display turns the picture book into a generic SaaS hero and erases the thesis that compute is told as a story.
- Don't use neutral grays such as #6b7280 or pure #000000 for text — off-palette grays read cold against the plum illustrations and break the tinted-ink rule.
- Don't put white text on the #f86d60 coral pill — the measured label is #281950, and white on coral drops contrast to roughly 2.8:1 while leaving the plum family.
- Don't make #6d28d9 Violet Ink the primary CTA fill — violet is the emphasis hue for italics, links and numerals, and promoting it collapses the two-hue budget into one.
- Don't frame illustrations in 24px cards with borders or shadows — the art is set at 0px radius directly on the canvas, and boxing it turns storybook drawings into stock thumbnails.
- Don't apply flat gray shadows like 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.25) — every system shadow is tinted rgba(40, 25, 80) at 14% or less, and black shadows muddy the lavender surfaces.
- Don't track body text or headlines positively — letter spacing above 0 belongs only to 12px uppercase labels (0.96px), and you should never widen anything larger.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- section band: #faf8ff (Lilac Mist)
- card fill: #ece9ff (Lavender Tile)
- primary text: #281950 (Plum Ink)
- body text: #5b4f78 (Slate Body)
- hairline: #e4def7 (Lilac Hairline)
- emphasis: #6d28d9 (Violet Ink)
- primary action: #f86d60 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts render the highlighted series as a solid #6d28d9 Violet Ink fill, comparison series in #e4def7 Lilac Hairline with #a39ac1 Heather Caption labels, and any secondary emphasis as Violet Ink at 20% opacity. Coral #f86d60 is excluded from data entirely so the CTA stays the warmest thing on the page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: an anchor styled as a pill with background #f86d60, text color #281950, border-radius 9999px, height 48px, padding 0 20px, font Fricolage Grotesque (fallback Bricolage Grotesque) at 15.5px weight 450 with 1.5 line height and 0 letter spacing, and box-shadow `inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(252, 185, 178, 1)`. Add a 12px chevron-right icon in #281950 with an 8px gap after the label. On hover, keep the fill and raise the inset ring to 2px. Place at most one per viewport.

2. Build a hero section: full-width container with a background gradient from #b8b6fb at the top left to #d9eef5 at the bottom (decorative, not system tokens), and inner content max-width 1200px with 160px top padding and 96px bottom padding. Left column 640px wide holds an h1 in Mackinac (fallback Fraunces at 450) at 56px weight 500, line-height 1.15, letter-spacing -1.68px, color #281950. Its second line is italic in #6d28d9. Below it, add a 19px Fricolage Grotesque paragraph at weight 325 in #5b4f78 with a 24px top margin, then a 32px gap to a row of a coral pill and a quiet text button (transparent, #5b4f78, 15px weight 450, radius 6px, padding 4px 12px). Bleed an unframed illustration off the right edge at 0px radius.

3. Build a use-case card grid: 3 columns with a 16px gap inside a 1200px container. Each card has background #e3f2f8 (top row) or #ece9ff (bottom row), no border, border-radius 24px, padding 32px, min-height 232px, and box-shadow `0 1px 2px 0 rgba(40, 25, 80, 0.04), 0 16px 40px -20px rgba(40, 25, 80, 0.14)`. The title is Mackinac 26px weight 500, line-height 1.25, letter-spacing -0.65px, color #281950. The description sits 16px below in Fricolage Grotesque 15px weight 325, line-height 1.5, color #5b4f78, max-width 240px. Replace one top-row cell with an unframed illustration and no card.

4. Build a navigation bar: a 96px-tall row, position relative and not sticky, transparent background, inner max-width 1200px. Put the logo left at 40px height. In the center, place a capsule with background rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.75), backdrop-filter blur(12px), border-radius 9999px, padding 4px, and box-shadow `0 0 0 1px rgba(32, 34, 55, 0.075), 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(32, 34, 55, 0.05), 0 4px 6px -4px rgba(32, 34, 55, 0.05)`. Fill it with links in Fricolage Grotesque 14.5px weight 450, color #281950, padding 10px 12px. On the right, place a matching capsule holding Log In (transparent, radius 20px 8px 8px 20px) and Sign Up (#f86d60 fill, #281950 text, radius 8px 20px 20px 8px, height 32px, padding 0 12px 0 10px, inset 1.5px rgba(252, 185, 178, 1) ring).

- **Section gap:** 96px (64–160px)
- **Card padding:** 32px (20–40px)
- **Element gap:** 16px (8–32px)

## Components

### Pill Button — Coral (Primary)

**Role:** The single conversion action per view

Warm, rationed, unmistakable. The spec: background #f86d60 Ember Signal, text #281950 Plum Ink rather than white, 1px border with no color, border-radius 9999px, padding 0 20px, height 48px, Fricolage Grotesque at 15.5px weight 450, and the sm-2 shadow `inset 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(252, 185, 178, 1)`. That inner ring draws a lighter coral edge, like a printed ticket stub. A trailing 12px chevron sits 8px after the label. Dark ink on coral is deliberately anti-convention, because most platforms put white on their brand fill, and this choice keeps the button inside the plum family.

### Pill Button — White (Secondary)

**Role:** The alternative path beside coral

Paper-white and pressed. The spec: background #ffffff Paper Canvas, text #281950, 1px border in violet at 12.5% alpha (#5b21b620, not a system token, so build with Lilac Hairline #e4def7), border-radius 9999px, padding 0 20px, height 48px, Fricolage Grotesque at 15.5px weight 450, and the subtle-2 shadow `inset 0 -3px 6px -2px rgba(231, 230, 244, 1)`. The inset gives the pill a soft bottom curl. Use it for "Talk to an engineer" next to the coral pill, where the shared geometry and the opposite fill make the hierarchy obvious.

### Pill Button — Ghost on Plum (Secondary, Dark)

**Role:** Secondary action inside the night band

Outlined and luminous. The spec: transparent background on #231850 Plum Night, text #ffffff, 1px border in Paper Canvas at 25% opacity, border-radius 9999px, padding 0 20px, height 48px, Fricolage Grotesque at 15.5px weight 450, and the sm shadow `0 5px 5px -2px rgba(91, 33, 182, 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgba(91, 33, 182, 0.1)`. A trailing chevron follows the label. The violet-tinted shadow keeps even the dark band's elevation in-family, so use this pill only on Plum Night and Plum Basement.

### Quiet Text Button — Icon Leading

**Role:** Tertiary action beside the hero CTA

A label with a 6px hit area. The spec: transparent background, text measured at #4a3f6b (not a system token, so build with Slate Body #5b4f78), no border, border-radius 6px, padding 4px 12px, height 31px, Fricolage Grotesque at 15px weight 450, no shadow, and a 14px copy icon 8px before the label. The 6px radius is the system's smallest and shows only on hover, which tells the reader this is a utility ("Onboard your agent") rather than a competing CTA.

### Split Auth Pair — Log In / Sign Up

**Role:** Account entry in the nav

The system outlier. Log In and Sign Up share a glass capsule with the lg shadow. Log In carries a 20px 8px 8px 20px radius, and Sign Up mirrors it at 8px 20px 20px 8px. Sign Up uses background #f86d60, text #281950, padding 0 12px 0 10px, height 32px, Fricolage Grotesque at 14.5px weight 450 and the sm-2 inset coral ring. The asymmetric corners break the pure-pill rule on purpose: together the two halves read as one pill split by an 8px seam, a physical toggle rather than two loose buttons.

### Floating Glass Nav Pill

**Role:** Primary site navigation, centered and floating

Frosted capsule, not sticky. The spec: a 96px nav row (position relative, so it scrolls away), logo left, auth pair right, and a centered link capsule with background Paper Canvas at 75% opacity, border-radius 9999px, shadow lg, and a backdrop blur over the hero gradient. Links are #281950 Plum Ink in Fricolage Grotesque at 14.5px weight 450 with padding 10px 12px and height 42px. Floating the links in a translucent pill instead of a full-width bar is intentional, because the illustrated sky stays visible behind the navigation.

### Mega Menu Panel

**Role:** Product taxonomy dropdown

Editorial index card. The spec: background #ffffff, border-radius 24px, shadow xl `0 24px 60px 0 rgba(40, 25, 80, 0.14)`, and four columns headed by uppercase eyebrows in #6d5f8f Pewter Label at Fricolage Grotesque 12px weight 500 with 0.96px tracking and padding 0 10px 8px. Each item is an inner tile with radius 10px and padding 8px 10px. Titles are #281950 at 14.5px weight 450, and descriptions are #5b4f78 at 14.5px weight 325. The deepest, widest shadow in the system is reserved for the one surface that actually floats over content.

### Use-Case Card — Frosted / Lavender (Main Content Card)

**Role:** The primary content tile

Pastel paper, softly lifted. The spec: background #e3f2f8 Frosted Tile for the top row and #ece9ff Lavender Tile for the bottom row, no border, border-radius 24px, padding 32px, shadow md `0 1px 2px 0 rgba(40, 25, 80, 0.04), 0 16px 40px -20px rgba(40, 25, 80, 0.14)`. The title is Mackinac at 26px weight 500 with -0.65px tracking in #281950, and the description is Fricolage Grotesque at 15px weight 325 in #5b4f78. Cards sit in a 3-column grid with 16px gaps, and one cell holds an unframed illustration. The negative-spread shadow pools beneath the card instead of haloing it, so the tiles feel set down on the page.

### Integration Logo Grid

**Role:** Partner and framework proof

A ruled specimen sheet. The spec: a white container with border-radius 24px and a 1px #e4def7 Lilac Hairline outline and internal dividers. It forms a 3-column grid of cells about 112px tall, each holding a 28px monochrome mark in #281950 above a label in Fricolage Grotesque at 14.5px weight 500. On Plum Night the same grid flips to translucent white at 10% alpha with white marks and white labels. Hairlines instead of separate cards make nine logos read as one catalogue page.

### Data Link List

**Role:** Product rows with arrows

A table of contents. The spec: full-width rows separated by 1px #e4def7 top and bottom rules, with 16px vertical padding per row. The name is #281950 in Fricolage Grotesque at 15px weight 500 in a 76px left column, the description is #5b4f78 at 14.5px weight 325, and a right-aligned 14px arrow uses #6d28d9 Violet Ink. There is no background, radius or shadow. This is how the system lists siblings (Postgres, Redis, Tigris, Volumes): rules and an arrow, the opposite of a card grid.

### Stat Trio

**Role:** Quantified social proof

Serif numerals in violet. The spec: three columns with 40px gaps, numerals in Mackinac at 40px weight 500 with 1.25 line height and -1px tracking in #6d28d9 Violet Ink, and captions below in Fricolage Grotesque at 14.5px weight 325 in #5b4f78. There is no background, card or border. Setting "1.6M+", "18" and "53%" in the book serif rather than a tabular sans is anti-convention, so the numbers read as storybook facts rather than dashboard metrics.

### Plum Footer

**Role:** Closing sitemap and newsletter

The deepest floor. The spec: background #191034 Plum Basement, text #a39ac1 Heather Caption in Fricolage Grotesque at 14.5px weight 325 with 1.65 line height, and padding 80px 0 32px. Column heads are uppercase 12px weight 575 with 0.6px tracking in #ffffff. A newsletter form uses inputs with an 8px radius, padding 8px 12px and height 40px on a field one tone above the floor, beside a violet Subscribe button with an 8px radius. The footer is the only place 8px rectangles cluster, a deliberate shift into utility mode.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in Mackinac at weight 500 with -0.025em tracking (-1.1px at 44px) — the medium serif is the storybook voice, and a single weight keeps hierarchy carried by size.
- Turn the second clause of hero headlines into italic Mackinac in #6d28d9 Violet Ink — the violet italic is the signature move and gives one emotional beat per page.
- Use purple-tinted neutrals for all text, with #281950 for titles, #5b4f78 for body and #a39ac1 for captions — tinted ink is non-negotiable because it ties copy to the illustrations.
- Reserve #f86d60 Ember Signal for at most one pill per viewport, sized at 48px height with a 9999px radius — scarcity makes coral read as the ticket, not as decoration.
- Lift content cards with the md shadow (0 16px 40px -20px at 14% plum) and a 24px radius — the negative spread pools shadow under the card like paper on a desk.
- Separate sections with surface shifts between #ffffff, #faf8ff and #231850 at 96px gaps — tonal banding replaces dividers and keeps the page rhythm calm.
- Write body copy in Fricolage Grotesque at weight 325 and 17px with 1.5 line height — the light grotesk lets the serif headlines carry all the visual weight.

### Don't

- Don't bold headlines to 700 or switch them to a sans — a heavy grotesk display turns the picture book into a generic SaaS hero and erases the thesis that compute is told as a story.
- Don't use neutral grays such as #6b7280 or pure #000000 for text — off-palette grays read cold against the plum illustrations and break the tinted-ink rule.
- Don't put white text on the #f86d60 coral pill — the measured label is #281950, and white on coral drops contrast to roughly 2.8:1 while leaving the plum family.
- Don't make #6d28d9 Violet Ink the primary CTA fill — violet is the emphasis hue for italics, links and numerals, and promoting it collapses the two-hue budget into one.
- Don't frame illustrations in 24px cards with borders or shadows — the art is set at 0px radius directly on the canvas, and boxing it turns storybook drawings into stock thumbnails.
- Don't apply flat gray shadows like 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.25) — every system shadow is tinted rgba(40, 25, 80) at 14% or less, and black shadows muddy the lavender surfaces.
- Don't track body text or headlines positively — letter spacing above 0 belongs only to 12px uppercase labels (0.96px), and you should never widen anything larger.

## Imagery

Imagery is hand-drawn illustration, not photography or product screenshots, and that is the defining asset after the serif. Inked line art with grainy risograph-style fills shows hot-air balloons, floating islands under glass domes, a rocket-propelled server cube, a lavender elephant and a planet surface. The palette is lilac, coral, teal and violet, and the illustration hexes are decorative, not system tokens. Images sit unframed at 0px radius directly on the canvas or bleed off the right edge of the hero, with no border, container surface or shadow. Icons are monochrome Plum Ink brand marks at 28px in the integration grid, plus simple 14px stroke chevrons and arrows in Violet Ink. The hero uses a soft periwinkle-to-ice sky gradient and the night band carries a fine noise texture, both decorative backdrops rather than tokens. The narrative is whimsical exploration: deploying to Fly is an expedition across an illustrated sky.

## Layout

Content holds to a 1200px max-width with text measures between 416px and 640px. Sections stack at a 96px default gap, opening to 160px around the hero and tightening to 64px inside bands. The hero is left-aligned: a 56px serif headline over a 19px subhead and a coral-plus-quiet button pair, with a full-bleed illustration occupying the right and lower half. Sections then alternate between white and #faf8ff with split two-column compositions (heading left, grid right), interrupted by one #231850 night band. Feature cards use a 3-column grid, integration grids use 3 columns, stats use 3 columns, and the customer logo row is a horizontal marquee of about 10 marks. The nav is 96px, not sticky, and transparent over the hero, with the logo left, a glass link capsule centered and the split auth pair right. The footer is a multi-column #191034 sitemap with a newsletter form. At 375px, set display to 44px, set section gaps to 64px and stack every grid to 1 column. Density is comfortable.

## Storybook Serif Discipline

The discipline is that a single book serif at weight 500 carries every headline, card title and numeral, while illustration carries the mood. It breaks the moment anyone adds a second display face, bolds Mackinac to 700, or sets a section title in Fricolage Grotesque to "feel more technical." At that point the picture-book framing collapses into the 700-weight sans convention that every other cloud platform already uses. It also breaks when the violet italic multiplies: one italic clause per hero is punctuation rather than decoration, but three per page become a gimmick. To extend the system, add new heading sizes only on the existing -0.025em tracking line, keep weight 500 fixed, and reserve italics in #6d28d9 for a single turn of phrase per view.

## Tinted Neutral Discipline

There is no gray in this system. Every neutral, from #281950 Plum Ink through #5b4f78, #6d5f8f, #a39ac1 and #e4def7, carries a violet hue, and every shadow is tinted rgba(40, 25, 80). That is anti-convention against the slate and zinc ramps of utility frameworks. It breaks when a component imports a stock gray border, a black 25% shadow, or #6b7280 helper text, because the cold patch reads instantly against the lavender illustrations. To extend it, derive any new neutral by mixing #281950 into #ffffff at a fixed percentage, so the hue stays constant and only lightness moves. New dark surfaces should step from #231850 toward #191034 rather than toward true black.

## Coral Rationing

Ember Signal #f86d60 appears on exactly 3 elements on the entire home page, and each is a conversion pill. That ratio is the system's conversion engine, since nothing else on the page is warm and saturated, so the eye lands on coral without being told. It breaks when coral leaks into icons, badges, link hovers, chart series or alert banners, because each extra use dilutes the ticket. Warnings and errors must not borrow it either; they need their own status tone, added to the color table first. To extend the system, give every new action a white or ghost pill. Promote an action to coral only when it starts an account, and keep the #281950 label and the 1.5px inset ring intact.

## Similar Brands

- **Mailchimp** — shares the pairing of a medium-weight editorial serif with hand-drawn, grainy brand illustration, though Mailchimp leads with a saturated yellow where Fly.io leads with lavender.
- **Heroku** — shares the purple-anchored developer PaaS palette and night-plum surfaces, but uses a sans display and flat icons where Fly.io uses a book serif and narrative art.
- **Stripe** — shares hue-tinted neutrals instead of grays and a violet emphasis color, but builds depth with gradients and product UI rather than storybook drawings.
- **Railway** — a direct category competitor deploying apps on managed infrastructure, with purple-violet accents. Railway commits to a dark theme, while Fly.io keeps a light canvas with a single night band.
- **Notion** — shares the use of inked spot illustrations to humanize a technical product, but stays monochrome where Fly.io budgets two saturated hues.
